To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed storage placement and replica placement mechanism can be implemented in content-centric publish-subscribe networks to store content and provide a differentiated storage and replica assignment for different content types.

(i) the proposed storing mechanism and replica assignment algorithm provide a good trade-off between storage utilization and response latency, (ii) the proposed replica assignment algorithm provides a better response latency than the proposed replica assignment algorithms and (iii) the proposed storing mechanisms and replica assignment algorithm are scalable and provide a good tradeoff between storage utilization and network traffic, even in a dynamic scenario.

A novel storage placement and replica placement algorithm is proposed that enables storing in publish/subscribe networks and minimizes the response time of clients, the overall network traffic and the number of servers in the network, compared to a greedy (optimal) approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of a storage placement and replica allocation algorithm in content-centric publish-subscribe networks.
the design and implementation of an efficient storage placement and replica management scheme for content-centric publish/submit networks.
the design, implementation and evaluation of a content storage and replica assignment mechanism for content-centric publish/ subscribe networking.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed storage placement and replica allocation mechanism performs as close as to the greedy (near optimal approach) in the context of publish/subscribe content distribution networks.
our proposed solution is a very promising one, which can be used in content-centric networks, and that the proposed storage placement and replica placement algorithms perform very well.

the proposed storage placement and replica algorithm performs very well, even in the case of a high locality of users requests, while the proposed storage mechanism is very close to a greedy (optimal) approach, but installs less storage servers in order to achieve the desired differentiation among the classes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel storage placement and replica allocation mechanism that is able to differentiate among classes of content, based on their popularity, and to optimize the storage placement and the replica allocation, while at the same time it provides the necessary differentiation among classes of content.
our proposed mechanism is able to provide content storage, while maintaining the loose coupling and asynchronous communication of publish/subscribe networking.
the proposed mechanism and algorithm provide a good tradeoff between the storage cost and the performance of the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a content-centric publish/ subscribe system with a storage and replica assignment scheme that differentiates content based on their importance can be implemented in a network with limited resources and can provide the necessary differentiation among classes of the content, while maintaining the loose-coupled nature of the network and providing a low latency to clients.

the proposed mechanism is able to provide the required differentiation between the content classes and is capable of reducing the number of storage nodes by up to 3x while providing the necessary storage differentiation among content classes.
the proposed mechanism is able to provide a trade-off between the performance of the network and the storage capacity of its components.
